title: Huang resigns, Kress steps in at Nvidia — open models lose a patron
summary: Jensen Huang resigned as Nvidia's CEO and CFO Colette Kress took over as interim, with a congressional hearing, a Democratic letter on chip-export dealings and Tuesday's earnings ahead. Then what Huang's exit means for open models and the pending Hugging Face deal, and the AI-crash case built from this week's financing: Nebius's delays, SoftBank's turbine write-down and Nvidia's circular deals.

topics: Jensen Huang resigns from Nvidia (12 November 2026): board says 'resigned as president, CEO, and member of the board, effective immediately'; TechCrunch says 'ousted'; CFO Colette Kress interim CEO (Nvidia since Sept 2013, ex-Cisco, 13 years Microsoft), 'more thorough search' under way; Oppenheimer 'massive shoes to fill and no obvious successor'; Fedasiuk: distraction is the risk; Huang agrees to closed-door House testimony by Thanksgiving (Mast: 'some very serious questions to answer'); Reuters reports a third affair (unnamed employee); Neal/Wyden letter to Lutnick on H200-via-US tariff 'scheme', 'unconstitutional export tax system'; Trump floats Tim Cook ('A Legend replaces a Legend!'); earnings Tuesday 17 November.

Nvidia's open-source patronage after Huang: pending $12.9B Hugging Face acquisition (close H1 2027, DOJ questions per Reuters), Nemotron, $6B Poolside license, Reflection AI/Thinking Machines investments, July open-weights letter (25 companies); insider says Nemotron unaffected; Lambert 'very very bad for the open model cause in the US'; Delangue 'This whole thing sucks... we'll keep fighting for open-source AI, harder than ever.' Ada: the risk was one patron owning the neutral shelf; Alan: somebody has to pay for the commons, keep local copies. Unresolved.

The AI-crash case from this week's financing (Economist leader paywalled, not read): Nebius 2027 capex $40-45B, up to 85% via prepayments and contract-backed loans, 2026 forecast cut $200M to $3B on third-party site delays, Microsoft contract up to $19.4B with termination right, Vineland NJ partial delay, DataOne fined $1.1M, stock -17%, Q3 revenue $981M +571%; SoftBank $7.1B quarterly loss, >$3B on >13 GW of turbines ordered ~50% over need, Gardett 'price discovery'; Nvidia ~$750B circular deals (Bloomberg via TechCrunch), $105B Ohio backstop (CNBC), ~half of ~$80B data center bonds junk (Forbes). Ada: watch the chain, trouble starts as a delay; Alan: prepayments are real demand.

dives.why_it_matters: Nvidia investors and anyone buying its chips care because the company that sets AI's hardware pace now has an interim finance chief as CEO, a congressional hearing and an earnings call within days.
Open-weight builders and local-LLM users care because the industry's loudest backer of open models left while his company is midway through buying the main platform those models are distributed on.

Investors and compute buyers care because this week's filings show the AI build-out's financing chain — prepayments, contract-backed loans, turbine deposits, chipmaker-financed customers — and where delays are already biting.
